title: Fixing the coin recovers the randomised run
statement: Let $p$ be a one-way public-coin protocol with shared-randomness type $\Omega$, input types $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$; let $\omega \in \Omega$ be a coin outcome and $x \in X$, $y \in Y$ be inputs. Fixing the public coin at $\omega$ turns $p$ into a deterministic one-way protocol, and executing that deterministic protocol on inputs $x$ and $y$ yields the same output as running $p$ on the joint inputs $(\omega, x)$ for Alice and $(\omega, y)$ for Bob. In both cases the output is Bob's decoder applied to his input $(\omega, y)$ together with the message that Alice's encoder assigns to $(\omega, x)$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a one-way public-coin protocol with randomness type Ω, input types X, Y, and output type α
ω ∈ Ω is a fixed coin outcome
replaced:
For any public-coin protocol $p$, coin outcome $\omega$, and inputs $x \in X$,
$y \in Y$,
\[
  (p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}(\omega)).\mathrm{run}(x, y)
  \;=\;
  p.\mathrm{rrun}(x, y, \omega).
\]
That is, running the derandomised protocol on $(x,y)$ agrees with running the
randomised protocol on $(x,y)$ with fixed randomness $\omega$.
